title: Compaction follows compression.threshold again: no default 256K token cap
before: At parent 5912ed81ed945a784f67ca13c1096e2c122cd307, the canonical compression configuration set compression.threshold_tokens to 256000 and the schema version to 46. When the raw compression section omitted the key, agent construction fell back to that default and passed it as the compressor's absolute threshold cap. The compressor then used the lower of the ratio-derived trigger and the cap, so a 1M-token window with the default 0.50 ratio compacted at 256K rather than 500K; an explicit null was already an opt-out. The example configuration was version 46 and materialized threshold_tokens: 256000, and the shared seeding path copied that template into new configurations, turning the temporary default into a persisted literal that looked like a user choice. Existing gateway-cache and TUI hot-reload consumers also resolved an absent key through DEFAULT_CONFIG, so they treated absence as the 256K cap.
after: At 98278833e29b167fe930e276eed7cb16bee68673, compression.threshold_tokens is None in DEFAULT_CONFIG and the schema/template move to version 47. An absent key now constructs a compressor with no absolute cap, so the ratio- and model-derived trigger governs across context-window sizes; a positive user-supplied cap remains supported, is applied as the lower-of ratio-versus-absolute rule, and survives model switches. The new v47 migration removes threshold_tokens only when a versioned pre-v47 configuration contains exactly the stale 256000 default; other explicit caps and explicit null remain untouched. Because the gateway cache signature and TUI live-sync code already read the canonical default, their behavior follows the new policy: absent and explicit null are ratio-only, while an explicit positive cap remains a distinct cached/live configuration. Documentation and regression expectations now describe the absolute cap as opt-in.
diff: The commit changes 10 files with 73 insertions and 66 deletions. The production policy change is the DEFAULT_CONFIG flip from 256000 to None plus config schema v46 to v47; the example template becomes a commented optional cap and v47. A new v46-to-v47 migration uses the existing stale-default rewrite mechanism to delete only the exact old literal. The compressor algorithm, gateway cache extraction, and TUI live-sync implementation are not structurally changed because they already derive their fallback from DEFAULT_CONFIG; their tests are updated to assert the new default while preserving explicit-cap behavior. Three documentation pages are updated from a universal 256K cap to an optional absolute cost ceiling.

    * feat(core): preload deferred tools within a context-window threshold
    
    Adds tools.toolSearch.threshold (default 10, percent of the context
    window). At session start, when the combined estimated schema footprint
    of every deferred tool - bundled built-ins and MCP alike - fits within
    the budget, all are revealed upfront so the declaration list stays
    stable for the whole session and prefix KV caches survive; otherwise
    everything stays deferred. Set 0 to always defer. Mirrors Claude Code's
    ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto threshold mode, extended to bundled deferred
    tools because here every reveal rewrites the declaration list and busts
    the prompt-cache prefix.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(core): log deferred-tool preload budget decision
    
    Emit debugLogger diagnostics in preloadDeferredToolsWithinBudget covering
    the computed budget, estimated token footprint, candidate count, and which
    branch of the all-or-nothing gate was taken (no candidates, over budget, or
    preloaded). Lets an operator diagnosing session-startup cost tell from debug
    logs whether the deferred set fit the budget or was left behind ToolSearch,
    without adding temporary instrumentation. No behavior change.
    
    * fix(tools): bound toolSearch.threshold to 0-100%
    
    The threshold setting is a percentage of the context window but had no
    upper bound, so a value like 200 (a typo or misreading of the "(%)"
    label) made the preload budget exceed the whole window and
    unconditionally preloaded every deferred tool — the opposite of the
    prefix-stability the threshold buys.

      like autoCompactThreshold) and regenerate the VS Code settings schema.
    - Add a symmetric runtime upper guard next to the existing
      'thresholdPercent <= 0' lower guard in client.ts, clamping to 100% so a
      hand-edited settings file cannot slip a larger budget past validation.
    
    Adds a client test asserting a 200% threshold clamps to a full-context
    budget.
    
    * test(core): cover configured preload budget
    
    * fix(tool-search): harden preload threshold
    
    * test(tool-search): cover preload exclusions

Core ConfigParameters accepts a toolSearchThreshold percentage, Config stores it with a default of 10, and getToolSearchThreshold exposes the effective value to runtime consumers.
The CLI config assembly passes settings.tools.toolSearch.threshold into ConfigParameters and supplies 0 instead when bareMode or safeMode is active.
The settings schema defines the deferred-tool threshold as a number with default 10 and a JSON-schema minimum of 0 and maximum of 100; the generated VS Code schema mirrors type, bounds, and default.

The session-start budget adapter skips when ToolSearch is absent, the threshold is non-finite or non-positive, or the context window is invalid; otherwise it clamps the percentage to 100, selects configured contextWindowSize or tokenLimit(model,'input'), and passes floor(contextWindow*boundedPercent/100) to the registry.
The model input-token-limit helper returns a known model limit when available and otherwise falls back to DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT, which is the fallback used by the client budget adapter.

Existing revealed candidates remain in the candidate set and therefore count toward the total.

The declaration path includes a deferred tool when it is not hidden; the hidden predicate requires shouldDefer, not alwaysLoad, not already revealed, and not listed in visibleTools. Therefore revealing a candidate makes its schema part of subsequent declarations, while always-loaded and visible tools do not need preload budget.

When ToolSearch is available, deferred-reminder setup filters out already-revealed tools; when ToolSearch is unavailable, the existing branch eagerly reveals all deferred summaries and returns no reminder. title: perf(core): chat history O(n^2) re-serialization on every turn causes jank on long sessions
before: The pinned commit's parent was af687798afe3b83fd8bf46e91d659c88347427ba. In the parent implementation, the interactive tool coordinator appended combined cancellation function responses to the durable chat history even when all model-initiated tools in the turn were cancelled. The interactive and legacy execution paths could also finish after a tool continuation that produced no visible response. For invalid-stream retries, GeminiChat appended retry nudges to the system instruction rather than to the end of the current request contents. The edit self-correction path did not reject a blank search string before invoking the correction helper, and no-match feedback was less specific.
after: The interactive coordinator records a history-length checkpoint before sending a prepared query and truncates the current history back to that checkpoint when all model-initiated tools are cancelled, without appending cancellation responses or issuing another model request. Interactive continuations now detect empty post-tool output and submit a recovery nudge with a per-user-query budget of two automatic attempts. The legacy execution loop performs the corresponding post-tool empty-response recovery once per armed tool-response cycle. GeminiChat now keeps systemInstruction stable and applies invalid-stream retry nudges to request contents, preserving role alternation and reapplying the nudge after hook content replacement. The edit invocation rejects missing or whitespace-only old_string before LLM correction and returns more actionable exact-match guidance. The commit also adds outgoing empty-part normalization and a wording-only attribution cleanup.
diff: Commit 812f7a2bcf20b6e80e2e50c3c8fa8e26567bc1e8 changes nine files: interactive stream coordination and tests, legacy agent/session behavior and tests, GeminiChat retry/content handling and tests, and Edit-tool validation and tests. The semantic changes are bounded cancellation-history rollback, bounded recovery after silent tool continuations, end-of-context retry nudging, payload-part normalization, and early edit-input rejection. The available evidence contains regression tests for the primary rollback, recovery, retry-placement, and edit-guard paths, but no performance benchmark proving the reported O(n^2) symptom or a dedicated test for the new empty-part sanitizer.

candidate_atomics.name: rollback-cancelled-tool-turn
candidate_atomics.description: When every model-initiated tool in an interactive turn is cancelled, restore the conversation to the checkpoint taken before the current query instead of recording cancellation responses as a new user turn or sending another request.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent cancelled in-flight tool turns from persisting as transcript state and avoid unnecessary follow-up work.
semantic_action.pre_state: A prepared query has been sent, the model has appended a tool-call turn, all applicable model-initiated tools are terminally cancelled, and current history is longer than the saved query checkpoint.
semantic_action.post_state: History is truncated to the saved checkpoint; cancellation response parts are not appended and no continuation request is emitted.

candidate_atomics.name: bounded-interactive-post-tool-nudge
candidate_atomics.description: Recover an interactive continuation that follows tool execution but ends without visible text by issuing a bounded recovery nudge through the normal continuation path.

semantic_action.intent: Remove silent post-tool turns while bounding automatic recovery work.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continuation after tool execution finishes with no tool calls and no non-whitespace visible text; the current user query has fewer than two automatic nudge attempts.
semantic_action.post_state: A continuation request carrying the recovery nudge is submitted and the per-user-query counter is incremented; no automatic nudge is submitted after the two-attempt budget is exhausted.
semantic_action.validation: The interactive-hook test observes a second send containing the exact recovery nudge after an empty continuation.

candidate_atomics.name: bounded-session-post-tool-nudge
candidate_atomics.description: In the session execution loop, recover from an empty response immediately following completed tool calls by sending a dedicated nudge before allowing normal completion.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a tool-execution path from terminating without a user-facing explanation when the first post-tool response is empty.
semantic_action.pre_state: At least one tool call has completed, the next stream has no tool calls, and it emits no non-whitespace content.
semantic_action.post_state: The loop sends the recovery nudge as the next request, clears the armed-after-tool state, and continues; a visible response can then complete the session.

candidate_atomics.name: end-of-context-retry-nudge

semantic_action.pre_state: A retry follows a thought-only or no-response-text invalid stream; request contents may end in a model turn, an ordinary user turn, or a function-response user turn, and hooks may replace contents.

candidate_atomics.name: sanitize-empty-payload-parts

candidate_atomics.name: reject-blank-edit-search

semantic_action.pre_state: An edit invocation reaches self-correction with old_string missing or containing only whitespace.
semantic_action.post_state: Execution returns an INVALID_TOOL_PARAMS error without invoking the LLM edit fixer and tells the agent to inspect the target with ReadFile before supplying an exact search string.

candidate_atomics.name: clarify-edit-no-match-guidance
